topic: Sanji's rule about never hurting women is a choice, not the weakness Ivankov warned about; the real weakness is putting himself last
title: Sanji's Rule About Women Was Never His Weakness
description: Everyone jokes that women are Sanji's weakness, but Enies Lobby, Arlong Park and Fish-Man Island point somewhere else. Is the real weakness his kindness or his self-neglect?
comment: Is Sanji's real weakness his rule about women, or his habit of putting himself last? Pick one.

lines.text: Nobody noticed what Sanji's fight with Kalifa really proved about his weakness.

shot.fallback: cook facing a woman in glasses and a suit

lines.text: Chapters 402 and 403, Enies Lobby. Kalifa wins by using one thing: Sanji refuses to hurt a woman.
So everyone files it under weakness. I don't think that's what Ivankov meant.

shot.fallback: tall queen pointing at a young cook

lines.text: What does cost him is taking hits for other people. Chapter 86, he dives in after Luffy and nearly loses to Kuroobi.

shot.search: Sanji Kuroobi Luffy water Arlong Park
shot.fallback: cook diving into the sea after his captain

lines.text: That's the difference. The rule about women is a choice he makes. The self-neglect is a reflex.
A choice you can defend. A reflex you can't, and that's what the flashback at the end of chapter 1195 flags.
I think the real weakness was believing his own safety didn't count, and the women were just where it showed.
So what changes once that flaw finally switches off? Oda's answer is bigger than one fight.

shot.fallback: cook kicking with fire and dark lightning

lines.text: So the next time someone calls it his weakness, think about what nobody noticed...
